FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Divisional Council. 


Bensulfuron methyl, Technical is employed in the preparation of herbicidal formulations for agricultural use. 


Bensulfuron methyl is the accepted common name by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) for 
Methyl a-(4,6-dimethoxypyrimidin-2-ylcarbamoylsulfamoyl)-o-toluate. 


The empirical and structural formula and molecular mass of Bensulfuron Methyl are given below: 


Empirical Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass 


410.4 


l6 18 4-77

CH,—O O—C. 
re) — C H 3 


In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of /nsecticides Act, 1968 and 
the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the /nsecticides 
Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( second revision Y. The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard 


BENSULFURON METHYL, TECHNICAL — 
SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and methods 
of sampling and test for bensulfuron methyl, technical. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards, given below contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards. 


IS No. Title 

1070: 1992 Regent grade water (third revision) 

2362:1993 Determination of water by Karl 
Fischer method — Test method 
(second revision) 

6940: 1982 Method of tests for pesticides and 
their formulations (first revision) 

7601: 1983 Specification for fibreboard drums 


for general purposes (first revision) 


8190 (Part 1) Requirements for packaging of 


: 1988 pesticides: Part 1 Solid pesticides 
(second revision) 
10946:1996 Methods of sampling for technical 


grade pesticides (first revision) 
3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Description 
The material shall be in the form of white to pale yellow 


coloured homogenous powder, free from extraneous 
impurities and hard lumps. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with the requirements 
given in Table 1. 


4 PACKING 


The product shall be packed in fiber board drum with 
LDPE liner with suitable leak proof and pilfer proof 
closure system. The LDPE liner thickness shall not be 
less than 0.062 mm. Fiber board drum shall conform 


to IS 7601. The container shall also meet the general 
requirements given in IS 8190 (Part 1). 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The package shall bear legibly and indelibly 
the following information in addition to any other 
information as is necessary under Insecticides Act, 
1968 and Rules framed thereunder: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal bensulfuron methyl content, percent 
(m/m); 

h) Cautionary notice as worded in the /nsecticides 
Act, 1968, and Rules framed thereunder; and 


j) Any other information required under the Legal 
Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


6 SAMPLING 

Representative samples shall be drawn as prescribed in 
IS 10946. 

7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred to 
in col 4 and 5 of Table 1. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in the tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 17847 : 2022

( Clauses 3.2 and 7.1 )

ANNEX A 
[ Table 1, SI No. (i) ] 
DETERMINATION OF BENSULFURON METHYLCONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


Bensulfuron methyl content is determined by reverse 
phase liquid chromatography using isocratic system 
of elution. The eluted compounds are detected and 
quantified with an ultraviolet detector. The weight 
percent of bensulfuron methyl content in the sample 
is determined by comparing the peak area/height of 
bensulfuron methyl in the sample to that in the standard. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 High performance liquid chromatograph 
equipped with a constant temperature column 
compartment, a sample injector capable of injecting 
10 ul aliquots, a programmable variable wavelength 
ultraviolet detector and an integrator. The suggested 
operative parameters are as follows, but can be changed 
if necessary provided standardization is done. 


Column Zorbax SB C-8, 5 micron, 
4.6 x 250 mm stainless steel 
column 

Temperature 40 °C 

Mobile phase Acetonitrile : water 
(37 : 63 v/v), pH adjusted to 
2.7 with phosphoric acid 

Flow rate 2.0 ml/min. 

Detector UV detector (254 nm) 

Injection volume | 10 ul 


A-2.2 Analytical Balance 
A-2.3 Microlitre Syringe, 25 ul. 


A-2.4 Filtering Apparatus for Sample and Standard 
Solutions 


A-2.5 Ultrasonic Bath 

A-2.6 Standard Glassware 
A-2.7 Water Purification System 
A-3 REAGENTS 


A-3.1 Acetonitrile, HPLC grade. 
A-3.2 Water 


A-3.3 Benzanilide (Internal Standard), of known 
purity. 


A-3.4 Bensulfuron Methyl Reference Standard, of 
known purity. 


A-3.5 Ortho Phosphoric Acid, 85 Percent, HPLC 
grade. 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Preparation of Mobile Phase 


Add 370 ml of Acetonitrile to a 1 000 ml volumetric 
flask. Make up to volume with acidified water (pH 2.7). 
The solution is degassed. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Internal Standard 


Weigh accurately 50 mg of benzanilide into a 50 ml 
volumetric flask. Dissolve this in Acetonitrile and 
ultrasonicate for 10 min. Make up to volume with 
acetonitrile. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately 110 mg of bensulfuron methyl 
reference standard of known purity and add it into a 
50 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve this in acetonitrile 
and make up to volume and ultrasonicate for 10 mins. 
Pipettel0 ml aliquot from this solution into another 
100 ml volumetric flask and add 10 ml of benzanilide 
internal standard solution into the volumetric flask. 
Make up to volume with acetonitrile. 


A-4.4 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh accurately an amount of sample to contain 
110 mg of bensulfuron methyl and add it in to a 
50 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in acetonitrile and 
make up to volume and ultrasonicate for 10 min. 
Pipette 10 ml aliquot from this solution into another 
100 ml volumetric flask and add 10 ml of benzanilide 
internal standard solution into the same flask. Make up 
to volume with acetonitrile. 


A-4.5 Estimation 


A-4.5.1 Equilibrate the column with the mobile phase 
for 45 min before injecting the standard/sample. After 
the column has equilibrated and a stable baseline is 
obtained, inject, in duplicate, 10 ul each of standard 
and sample solution. 


A-4.5.2 Retention Time (Guide Values) 


Benzanilide (internal standard) - 7.0 min 
Bensulfuron methyl - 9.2 min 
Total run time - 12.0 min 


A-4.5.3 From the chromatograms of the standard 
solution and sample solution measure the peak areas 
of the active ingredient and the internal standard and 


IS 17847 : 2022 


calculate the percentage of the active ingredient as 
given in the calculation (A-5). 


A-5 CALCULATION 
Bensulfuron methyl content,percent by mass = 
M xI 
U, x percent purity of standard 
A, x M, x1, 
where 


M, — mass in g, of bensulfuron methyl standard; 


M,= mass in g, of the sample taken; 


A = peak area of bensulfuron methyl in the 
chromatogram of standard solution; 


I,— peak area of internal standard of bensulfuron 
methyl in the standard solution; 


A,= peak area of bensulfuron methyl in the 
chromatogram of sample solution; and 


I,— peak area of internal standard of bensulfuron 
methyl in the sample solution.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
